Search shows breadcrumbs still titled Gemini for Google Cloud Learning Path on related course pages.
Rubric prefers SKILL.md / Claude-Codex-Gemini CLI skills over course landing pages.
uncertainty: Current activity list, duration, and whether path 236 still exists as a first-class path.

aiReview.tagline: Official Google Cloud courses on Gemini in the console
aiReview.description: Follow Google’s structured Gemini for Google Cloud path with console labs, courses, and credentials on Google Skills.
pros: Hosted on Google Skills (formerly Cloud Skills Boost), an official Google training catalog.
The path covers Gemini features in Google Cloud with related courses such as Gemini for Data Scientists and Analysts.
Hands-on console labs and credentials are part of the platform, not a generic prompt dump.
cons: This is a human learning path, not an agent skill pack, SKILL.md, or CLI skill directory.
The canonical /paths/236 URL currently redirects to the Google Skills homepage, so the listing may be stale or remapped.
Access, labs, and credentials typically require a Google Skills account and may involve paid subscriptions or credits.

cons: The canonical URL is a course-session lab path that redirects to a sign-in page.
Content is not a SKILL.md pack, Claude/Codex/Gemini CLI skill, or skill directory.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Skills intermediate course on Gemini, Streamlit, and Cloud Run. It is a human lab/badge path, not an installable agent skill pack, so it is a weak fit for a skills-focused directory.
evidence: Canonical URL is a Google Skills course template (paths/236/course_templates/978).
Meta description and body cover Gemini prompting, function calls, Streamlit, Docker, and Cloud Run.
Rubric prefers agent skill packs over course landing pages.
uncertainty: Exact pricing and whether labs are free without a Skills subscription.
Full lab module list beyond the marketing description.
Whether challenge-lab content is accessible without prior course progress.
aiReview.tagline: Hands-on Gemini, Streamlit, and Cloud Run labs
aiReview.description: Learn Gemini prompting, Python SDK function calls, and deploying Streamlit apps as Docker containers on Cloud Run in an intermediate skill-badge course.
pros: Hosted on Google Skills with a stated intermediate skill-badge course and challenge lab.
Described scope includes text generation, Gemini API function calling with the Python SDK, Cloud Shell testing, and Cloud Run deployment.
Page lists a short duration (45 minutes) and a recent update timestamp.
cons: This is a course landing page, not a SKILL.md pack or CLI agent skill directory.
Hands-on labs typically require a Google Skills account and may not be freely usable without credits or a subscription.
No agent-installable skill files, prompts, or maintenance repo are provided on the page.

aiReview.summary: The canonical URL is a VoltAgent sponsor tracking link that redirects to SerpApi’s commercial search API homepage, not a SKILL.md pack or skill directory. Related agent skills exist elsewhere (e.g. officialskills.sh), but this candidate is a paid product landing page, not an installable agent skill.
evidence: Read of the candidate URL followed an alternate/feed path and did not serve a skill pack; search showed serpapi.com as a Google SERP API product.
VoltAgent/awesome-agent-skills README lists the URL as a sponsor with copy “Web Search API for your AI apps.”
README Skills by SerpApi section documents serpapi-web-search and agent-usability-test on officialskills.sh, plus GitHub tool/CLI repos, not this URL.
uncertainty: Exact current pricing tiers and free-tier limits were not verified on the live homepage.
Contents and maintenance of the officialskills.sh SerpApi SKILL.md files were not fetched.
Whether /awesome-agent-skills ever served dedicated skill docs vs. always redirecting is unverified.
aiReview.tagline: Paid SERP API for structured search results in apps
aiReview.description: Provides real-time search APIs across many engines, returning structured JSON. Requires an API key; not a SKILL.md skill pack.
pros: SerpApi is a documented commercial Web Search API used by AI apps, with JSON results and many engines.
The VoltAgent list separately points to two SerpApi-authored skills (web search and agent usability test) on officialskills.sh.
Companion GitHub repos exist for Python agent tools and a CLI covering 130+ engines.
cons: https://serpapi.com/awesome-agent-skills is a UTM sponsor redirect to the product homepage, not a skill repository or SKILL.md.
The candidate is a paid API service, not an installable Claude/Codex/Gemini skill pack.
Agent usefulness of this URL is low: no skill install path, maintenance signals, or SKILL.md content on the linked page.

aiReview.description: Install an agent skill that generates, edits, and extracts .docx content, including tables, tracked changes, headers, and TOC.

Describes concrete workflows: generate with docx-js, edit OOXML, extract with pandoc.
Use cases include reports, tracked changes, markdown extraction, and TOC templates.

aiReview.summary: Official Anthropic agent skill with a detailed SKILL.md that walks Claude through context gathering, section-by-section drafting, and reader testing for specs, RFCs, and similar docs. Installable via npx from anthropics/skills; useful for agents, not a standalone app.
evidence: canonicalUrl and GitHub tree skills/doc-coauthoring contain SKILL.md (~15KB).
Meta and page text: structured co-authoring with three stages and npx install.
Triggers include PRDs, design docs, decision docs, RFCs.
uncertainty: Ongoing maintenance cadence of the skill pack was not verified beyond current main branch.
Effectiveness of reader-testing without sub-agents was not evaluated in use.
aiReview.tagline: Three-stage workflow for co-authoring specs and docs
aiReview.description: Guides agents through context gathering, section drafting with iteration, and context-free reader tests before sharing technical docs.
pros: Official Anthropic skill in anthropics/skills with a substantial SKILL.md.
Install path is documented (npx skills add with --skill doc-coauthoring).
Workflow covers context dump, section brainstorm/curation, and reader testing via sub-agents when available.
cons: Depends on Claude artifacts, files, or sub-agents; some stages fall back to manual user testing.
Directory listing is a mirror of GitHub rather than independent documentation.

Source is VoltAgent awesome-agent-skills curated listing
uncertainty: Exact SKILL.md contents, license, and last-commit freshness were not fetched from GitHub
Whether the skill is still maintained in anthropics/skills main

aiReview.description: Install an Anthropic agent skill that extracts, edits, and builds .pptx decks including slides, layouts, notes, and design.
pros: Listed as an official Anthropic skill under anthropics/skills with a GitHub tree path for skills/pptx.
Install command is given: npx skills add https://github.com/anthropics/skills --skill pptx.
Described scope covers extract, edit, and generate presentations including layouts and speaker notes.
cons: The directory page title/meta description is truncated (“Handles everything involving .”).
SKILL.md contents are not fully shown on the listing page, so maintenance and exact APIs are not verified here.

aiReview.summary: Official Anthropic agent skill for reading, writing, and editing Excel/CSV/TSV with pandas, openpyxl, and LibreOffice formula recalculation. Installable via npx skills add from anthropics/skills; useful for spreadsheet work in coding agents.
evidence: officialskills.sh lists it as official Anthropic data skill with GitHub tree skills/xlsx.
Meta and body describe Excel/tabular read-write plus LibreOffice formula checks.
Install via npx skills add from github.com/anthropics/skills.
uncertainty: Exact SKILL.md contents, license, and last-commit freshness were not fully loaded.
Runtime requirements (LibreOffice, Python versions) not verified in this environment.
aiReview.tagline: Read, write, and verify Excel and tabular files
aiReview.description: Reads, writes, and edits .xlsx, .xlsm, .csv, and .tsv using pandas and openpyxl, with LibreOffice recalculation to catch formula errors.
pros: Official Anthropic skill in the public anthropics/skills repo with a documented SKILL.md install path.
Covers xlsx, xlsm, csv, and tsv with pandas analysis and openpyxl formatting/formulas.
Describes LibreOffice-based recalculation to surface formula error cell locations before delivery.
Install command is explicit: npx skills add https://github.com/anthropics/skills --skill xlsx.
cons: Directory page truncates some copy and similar-skill recommendations include unrelated Binance skills.
Depends on LibreOffice and Python libraries, which may be heavy or unavailable in some agent runtimes.

aiReview.summary: Official Anthropic agent skill for PDF read/write, merge/split, OCR, and related Python/CLI tooling; installable from the anthropics/skills repo.

Meta description matches listed PDF operations.

uncertainty: License, last commit, and SKILL.md completeness were not verified on GitHub.
Runtime quality of generated PDF code was not tested.
aiReview.tagline: Agent skill for PDF extract, merge, OCR, and generation

uncertainty: Live SKILL.md contents, license, and commit recency were not fetched from GitHub.

aiReview.summary: Official Anthropic agent skill (SKILL.md) that directs frontend UI work toward a committed aesthetic instead of generic AI defaults. Installable from github.com/anthropics/skills via npx skills add.

officialskills.sh documents npx skills add https://github.com/anthropics/skills --skill frontend-design.

uncertainty: Cannot verify how often the skill is updated or how well current CLI agents load it.
Exact SKILL.md instructions were not fully expanded on the catalog page.
aiReview.tagline: Commit to a visual tone before generating frontend UI
aiReview.description: Guides agents to pick a distinct aesthetic first, then ship production HTML/CSS with typography, space, and motion instead of generic templates.
pros: Hosted in the official anthropics/skills repository with a SKILL.md file.
Install path is documented: npx skills add with --skill frontend-design.
Use cases are concrete: landing pages, dashboards, HTML/CSS layouts, and motion.
Includes LICENSE.txt alongside the skill definition.

Install path is documented (npx skills add and GitHub tree URL).

aiReview.summary: Official Anthropic agent skill with a SKILL.md pack that applies 10 named color/font themes (or generates a custom one) to slides, docs, reports, and HTML. Installable from anthropics/skills; useful for artifact styling, not a general coding toolkit.

officialskills.sh documents the same install command and GitHub tree URL.
Skill lists Ocean Depths through Midnight Galaxy and requires showing theme-showcase.pdf before apply.
uncertainty: LICENSE.txt terms were not fully reviewed in this pass.
Maintenance cadence of the skill pack beyond the public main-branch files is not verified.
aiReview.tagline: Apply 10 palettes or generate custom artifact themes
aiReview.description: Style slides, docs, reports, and HTML with 10 preset color/font themes or generate a custom theme from a description.
pros: Lives in the official anthropics/skills repo with a SKILL.md, themes/ files, and theme-showcase.pdf.

Names 10 themes and instructs the agent to read theme files and apply colors/fonts consistently.

cons: Scope is styling artifacts, not a broad coding or production-app skill.

# Modem skills

Agent skills from [Modem](https://modem.dev).

## Skills

### [`write-discoverable-code`](./write-discoverable-code/)

Rules for writing code that coding agents (and humans) can find through plain-text search: distinctive names, precise types, comments where search lands, and concept-named modules.

Distilled from Modem’s [How coding agents read your code](https://modem.dev/blog/how-coding-agents-read-your-code) post and the experiments behind it. This is skill **v4** from those runs.

## Install

Copy a skill directory into your agent’s skills folder:

```bash
# Cursor (project)
cp -R write-discoverable-code .cursor/skills/

# Claude Code (project)
cp -R write-discoverable-code .claude/skills/
```

Or clone this repo and point your harness at the skill path you want.

## Experiment data

Methodology, generated codebases, and run results live in the private [`code-writing-data`](https://github.com/modem-dev/code-writing-data) repo.

## License

[MIT](./LICENSE)

# Venice Skills

Agent Skills for the [Venice API](https://docs.venice.ai). Skills are self-contained folders of instructions (one `SKILL.md` each) that an LLM agent loads on demand to work correctly against a specific surface area of the API.

This repository is the canonical source of truth for Venice skills and is kept in sync with [`swagger.yaml`](https://docs.venice.ai). Use it with Cursor, Claude, Codex, Cline, or any other agent runtime that supports the Agent Skills format.

## What's in here

```
skills/        One folder per skill, each with a SKILL.md
template/      Copy this as a starting point for a new skill
```

## Skill catalog

| Skill | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`venice-api-overview`](./skills/venice-api-overview/SKILL.md) | Base URL, auth modes, response headers, pricing model, versioning |
| [`venice-auth`](./skills/venice-auth/SKILL.md) | Bearer API keys + SIWX / x402 wallet authentication (Base and Solana) |
| [`venice-chat`](./skills/venice-chat/SKILL.md) | `/chat/co

Agent Skills are an [open standard](https://agentskills.ai) for packaging expertise as instructions that AI agents can follow.

**Traditional content:** You read it → You apply it → You forget half of it.

**Agent Skills:** Your agent reads it → Your agent applies it → Every time. Perfectly.

Think of it like giving Claude Code a playbook written by an expert. Instead of prompting from scratch every time, the skill provides the framework, questions, and output format automatically.

# Mailtrap user skills

Agent skills for [Mailtrap](https://mailtrap.io) end users and builders using LLM-assisted coding. They summarize product flows, API bases and paths, and links to official documentation. They are not a substitute for [docs.mailtrap.io](https://docs.mailtrap.io/) or the [developer API documentation](https://docs.mailtrap.io/developers/).

## Standard

These skills follow the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) open standard (Anthropic, Dec 2025). Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) plus Markdown instructions. Compliant agents read only the frontmatter at startup and pull the body on demand (progressive disclosure), so the same folder works across multiple tools.

# Finding-Unknowns Skills

**14 installable skills that help your coding agent find what you don't know — before it gets expensive to fix.**

The map is not the territory. Your prompt is a map; the codebase and the real world are the territory. The gap between them is your *unknowns*, and with strong models the quality of the work is bottlenecked by how well you clarify them. The original eight task-level skills turn that idea, from [Thariq Shihipar's](https://thariqs.github.io/html-effectiveness/unknowns/) essay *A Field Guide to Fable: Finding Your Unknowns*, into commands you can run in Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Kimi Code CLI (Kimi K3), or any agent that reads the [agentskills.io](https://agentskills.io) SKILL.md format.

Another three come from his follow-up, [*The new rules of context engineering for Claude 5 generation models*](https://claude.com/blog/the-new-rules-of-context-engineering-for-claude-5-generation-models), which works one layer up: not the unknowns in a single prom

# Mental Models for Claude Code

Mental models as files an agent reads — bring your own, or start with the 21 that ship.

> A latticework for better decisions, one prompt away.

## What It Does

Ask for "inversion," "find the bottleneck," or "help me think through X" and Claude picks
2–4 models from different areas, walks their Thinking Steps against your actual problem,
surfaces the conditions under which each one misleads you, and tells you where they disagree.

The models are files. Twenty-one ship with it — each with a `sources` block whose claims
trace to something real — and you can add your own, which take precedence. No dependencies,
no runtime, no build step.

## Install

**Claude Code — plugin (recommended):**

```bash
/plugin marketplace add cyperx84/claude-skills-mental-models
/plugin install mental-models@mental-models
```

Or from your shell:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add cyperx84/claude-skills-mental-models
claude plugin install mental-models@mental-models
```

# dev-agent-skills

Agent skills and hooks for development workflows - Git, GitHub, skill authoring, safety guardrails, public-repo privacy, and decision records.

These skills are designed for [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code), the CLI tool by Anthropic.

## Why these skills?

Claude Code already knows how to commit, create PRs, and review code. But without structured guidance it tends to:

- Use inconsistent commit formats across a session
- Skip target branch confirmation and create PRs against the wrong branch
- Not search for task documentation or validate task completion before opening a PR
- Suggest labels that don't exist in the project
- Process review comments in random order instead of by severity
- Use the wrong GitHub API syntax for replying to threads (`-f` instead of `--input -`)
- Generate verbose merge messages that clutter the git log
- Merge without verifying all review comments have been addressed

These skills add structured workflows that prevent these

# Swift Server Skills & Linting

A collection of Claude skills for guidance on Swift (Server) development, along with a linting tool that enforces best practices.

## The Technique

Claude, as any LLM (or Human) makes mistakes. When Claude makes a mistake, most people have one of two reactions:
- Tell Claude it sucks, and let it try again.
- Open up some social media, and vent about how Claude sucks.

However, trying the same with Humans has proven extremely ineffective. *Humans bite back.*

### The solution

The solution is a pretty simple feedback loop:
1. Whenever you generate code, _read it_ before you commit.
2. If you see a mistake, try to articulate what should be improved and _why_.
3. Iterate 2. until you have a rationale Claude can follow easily.
4. Add the rationale with a small code sample to a Claude skill, to ensure future iterations have the same context.

And now the critical step: **Encode your newfound rule/skill as a linter rule.**

- Working code examples for common use cases

```bash
git clone https://github.com/pinkforest/threejs-playground.git
```

# dembrandt-skills

![Enterprise UX for every agent](dembrandt-skills.png)

**Enterprise UX secrets, now built into your AI agent.**

Your agent writes the component in seconds. It does not know the modal should be a drawer, or that the grey it picked fails contrast. These skills carry that judgment: what to do, and what breaks otherwise. Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot and any agent that reads the Open Agent Skills format.

```bash
npx skills add dembrandt/dembrandt-skills --all
```

```
Review this interface for usability issues.
```

# Agent Skills for Context Engineering

A comprehensive, open collection of Agent Skills focused on context engineering and harness engineering principles for building production-grade AI agent systems. These skills teach the art and science of curating context, designing agent operating loops, and evaluating agent behavior across any agent platform.

## What is Context Engineering?

Context engineering is the discipline of managing the language model's context window. Unlike prompt engineering, which focuses on crafting effective instructions, context engineering addresses the holistic curation of all information that enters the model's limited attention budget: system prompts, tool definitions, retrieved documents, message history, and tool outputs.

# Transloadit Skills

This repo hosts agent skills for Transloadit.

If you’re a developer/agent consuming this repo, start with the `transloadit` router skill and then jump into a specific `docs-*`, `transform-*`, or `integrate-*` skill.

This repo is compatible with the `skills` installer CLI (https://skills.sh/).

Browse what’s available:
```bash
npx -y skills add https://github.com/transloadit/skills --list
```

Install into this project (or use `-g` for user-level):
```bash
npx -y skills add https://github.com/transloadit/skills --all
```

Install a single skill (direct path):
```bash
npx -y skills add https://github.com/transloadit/skills/tree/main/skills/docs-transloadit-robots
```

Local dev (already cloned):
```bash
npx -y skills add ./skills --list

YouTube Skills gives your AI agent instant access to **YouTube transcripts**, **video search**, **channel data**, and **playlist extraction**. claude plugin marketplace add getsentry/skills

```

```bash
claude plugin marketplace update
claude plugin update sentry-skills@sentry-skills
```

Or run `/plugin` to open the plugin manager.

# Gemini API skills

A library of skills for the Gemini API, SDK and model interactions.

## About

LLMs have fixed knowledge, being trained at a specific point in time. Software
dev is fast paced and changes often, where new libraries are launched every day
and best practices evolve quickly.

This leaves a knowledge gap that language models can't solve on their own. For
example, models don't know about themselves when they're trained, and they
aren't necessarily aware of subtle changes in best practices (like [thought
circulation](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thought-signatures)) or SDK
changes.

[Skills](https://agentskills.io/) are a lightweight technique for adding
relevant context to your agents. This repo contains skills related to building
apps powered by the Gemini API.

### Performance

generate correct API code following best practices to 87% with Gemini 3 Flash
and 96% with Gemini 3.1 Pro. F

Reusable agent skills maintained by [YYLO](https://yylo.dev). This repository is the canonical, independently versioned source for skills used by YYLO CLI, YYLO Ledger and YYLO Benchmark.

## Install

Install interactively with the open `skills` CLI:

```bash
npx skills add yylo-dev/yylo-skills
```

Install all skills for Claude Code, Codex, and Pi without prompts:

```bash
npx skills add yylo-dev/yylo-skills --skill '*' -a claude-code -a codex -a pi --copy -y
```

Install one skill by user-intent-first name:

```bash
npx skills add yylo-dev/yylo-skills --skill wiki-yylo
```

# Codex Skills

Reusable skills for ChatGPT work and Codex.

## Orchestrate

[`orchestrate`](orchestrate) encourages Codex to delegate large-scope work across focused agents, then integrate their results. Trivial tasks stay with the coordinator.

The pattern comes from [Practical multi-agent orchestration in Codex](https://x.com/pvncher/status/2080707291603407077).

### Install

Copy the skill into your personal Codex skills directory:

```sh
mkdir -p ~/.codex/skills
cp -R orchestrate ~/.codex/skills/orchestrate
```

Then invoke it explicitly with `$orchestrate`, or let Codex select it when a task calls for multi-agent coordination.

# guard-skills

Focused **guard skills** for coding agents: second-pass quality gates that catch the systematic failure modes of AI-generated code, tests, and docs before they ship.

Best use: let your agent do the work, then invoke the relevant guard on the diff before you present, commit, or merge it. These skills can guide writing when you explicitly ask for that, but they are strongest as reactive review passes.

Browse the package first:

```bash
npx skills add amElnagdy/guard-skills --list
```

Install the package:

```bash
npx skills add amElnagdy/guard-skills
```

# Agent Skills

[中文文档](README_CN.md)

A collection of AI agent skills — self-contained knowledge bases that can be loaded by AI coding assistants (e.g., Claude Code, Copilot CLI, Cursor) to gain expertise on specific topics.

## What is a Skill?

A skill is a structured Markdown document with YAML frontmatter that serves as a comprehensive reference on a topic. AI agents load skills to provide more accurate, context-aware assistance without needing to search documentation in real time.

Each skill lives in its own directory under `skills/<name>/` and consists of:

- **`SKILL.md`** — Entry point with frontmatter metadata and a quick-reference guide
- **`references/`** — Modular deep-dive files for detailed syntax, edge cases, and workflows

## Available Skills

| Skill                            | Description

reference.excerpt:
# ArrowSpace Skills

Portable skill definitions for working with **ArrowSpace** — a spectral vector search library that goes beyond cosine similarity by incorporating graph Laplacian eigenstructure.

> ArrowSpace adds a spectral dimension to vector similarity, enabling search that considers both semantic content and structural role in the dataset.

## Quick Start

```bash
uv pip install "arrowspace>=0.30.0"
```

Then:

```python
from arrowspace import ArrowSpaceBuilder
import numpy as np

items = np.array([[0.1, 0.2, 0.3], [0.0, 0.5, 0.1], [0.9, 0.1, 0.0]], dtype=np.float64)
graph_params = {"eps": 0.5, "k": 12, "topk": 6, "p": 2.0, "sigma": None}
aspace, gl = ArrowSpaceBuilder().build(graph_params, items)

query = np.array([0.05, 0.2, 0.25], dtype=np.float64)
hits = aspace.search(query, gl, tau=1.0)
print(hits)  # [(0, 0.99), (1, 0.76), (2, 0.22)]
```

The `graph_params` above are fallback defaults. Use [`arrowspace_tuner`](https://pypi.org/project/arrowspace-tuner/) to derive the base

evidence: README describes official PANews agent package with skills/panews, panews-creator, panews-web-viewer.
File tree includes SKILL.md, openai.yaml agents, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, .codex-plugin/plugin.json, src/commands, tests/cli.test.mjs, CI workflow.
License listed as MIT; README covers event pagination and Markdown content format.
uncertainty: Commit recency and CI health beyond the GitHub snapshot.
Whether creator APIs remain stable and require paid PANews accounts.
Real-world skill quality inside SKILL.md bodies beyond the README table.

aiReview.description: Install agent skills and plugins for PANews crypto news, public Polymarket boards, Markdown page reads, and authenticated article workflows.

aiReview.summary: MIT-licensed Agent Skills pack plus a story CLI for markdown fiction: story bible, drafting skills, and a continuity checker packaged for Claude Code, Codex, and SKILL.md agents. Well-documented, CI-backed, and installable via plugin marketplaces or npx skills add.
evidence: GitHub: 308 stars, 49 forks, MIT, JavaScript; README describes 24 skills and plugin install commands.
Repo includes .claude-plugin, .codex-plugin, docs/, evals/, bin/story.js, SECURITY.md, and GitHub workflows.
Listed from internet-dot/awesome-codex-plugins as Story Skills.
uncertainty: Live npm download volume and Scorecard numeric grade not independently verified in this pass.

aiReview.tagline: Markdown fiction skills with a continuity compiler for agent
aiReview.description: Plan and draft fiction in markdown with SKILL.md packs, Codex/Claude plugins, and a CLI that flags continuity errors.
pros: Ships SKILL.md skills plus official Claude Code and Codex plugin manifests.

MIT license, CI, CodeQL, Dependabot, OpenSSF Scorecard, docs, and evals/examples are present.
cons: Domain is fiction writing, not general software-engineering agent workflows.

aiReview.summary: Codex CLI skill that vendors a 15-workflow university teaching suite as one router skill with install-from-GitHub instructions; useful for agent skill directories but young (few stars/commits) and generated from a sibling Claude Code repo.

aiReview.tagline: Codex skill for the university teaching lifecycle
aiReview.description: Install a single Codex CLI skill that routes course design, assessment, delivery, and reflection workflows from natural language or ts-* aliases.

States it is generated from the Claude Code sibling via build_codex.py rather than hand-edited in place.
cons: Very small project signal: about 6 stars, 0 forks, and 4 commits on main.
Codex does not register slash commands; ts-* names are emulated aliases, which may confuse users expecting native commands.
Updates require deleting and reinstalling the skill rather than an in-place upgrade path.

aiReview.summary: MIT-licensed Claude Code/Codex skill pack with SKILL.md files, plugin install paths, and nine X/Twitter writing skills plus optional Publora/Apify/Pixfaro integrations. Suitable for an agent-skills directory; publishing still depends on third-party APIs and user approval.

Points to related skills, workflows, and custom skill authoring docs.
cons: Not a SKILL.md pack or installable skill directory; it is product documentation.
Command availability varies by plan, platform, and Claude Code version.
Some entries are removed, aliased, or gated behind subscriptions and cloud features.

Not an installable SKILL.md pack; usefulness depends on already using Claude Code.

aiReview.summary: Official Anthropic docs on using Agent Skills with the Messages API, including container parameters, Anthropic vs custom skills, and code-execution requirements. Strong fit as a canonical reference for skill installability and API usage.

States skills run in the code execution environment via container.skills with type, skill_id, and optional version.
Lists Anthropic skill IDs (pptx, xlsx, docx, pdf) and custom skill ID formats; links Skill Management API.

aiReview.description: Learn to attach pre-built and custom Agent Skills in the Messages API via containers and the code execution tool.
pros: Official Anthropic documentation covering Messages API integration for Agent Skills.
Documents prerequisites, skill sources (anthropic vs custom), version pinning, and up to 20 skills per request.
Includes multi-language request examples and links to Skills CRUD, versions, and authoring best practices.
cons: Requires a Claude API key and the code execution tool; not a standalone skill pack.
Title in the listing is generic (Skills API requirements) versus the page’s actual heading.

aiReview.summary: Official Claude Agent SDK docs on SKILL.md packs: filesystem discovery, invocation scoping, and slash-command dispatch in Python and TypeScript. Strong fit for an agent-skills directory.

Rubric prefers official Claude skills docs over news or prompt dumps; this is first-party Agent SDK skill documentation.

aiReview.description: Author SKILL.md files, load them from disk, scope which skills run, and dispatch named commands in Python and TypeScript sessions.
pros: Official documentation with Python and TypeScript examples for query() options, setting sources, and Skill tool allowlisting.
Explains filesystem layout (.claude/skills, user vs project), discovery, and model- vs user-invoked skills.
Covers slash-command dispatch, init-message inspection of loaded skills, and command vs SKILL.md successor notes.
cons: Skills are file-based only; there is no programmatic registration API.
Page is SDK-specific and points elsewhere for general authoring architecture.

aiReview.summary: Official Agent Skills documentation on eval-driven skill testing: test cases, with/without-skill baselines, assertions, grading, and iteration. Practical for maintainers, not an installable skill pack.

aiReview.description: Design test cases, run with/without-skill baselines, grade assertions, and iterate on SKILL.md using pass rates, timing, and human review.

Specifies evals.json, workspace layout, timing, grading, and benchmark.json patterns.
Covers baselines, assertion quality, pattern analysis, and iteration on SKILL.md.
cons: Tutorial resource, not an installable SKILL.md pack.
Workflow is manual and Claude Code–oriented (subagents, token notifications).

aiReview.summary: Official Anthropic announcement of skill-creator evals, benchmarks, multi-agent test runs, and description-tuning for Agent Skills. Useful context for skill authors, but it is a product article rather than an installable SKILL.md pack.
